statement: Nanostructured or melt-spun Bi-Sb-Te systems sustain zT >= 1.1 at 350 K.
rationale: Both SPS-nanostructured Bi0.3Sb1.7Te3 (zT 1.2) and melt-spun Bi2Te3 (zT 0.95) cluster near zT 1.0-1.2 at 350 K; the decoupling threshold separates texture-driven from intrinsic performance.

statement: Lattice thermal conductivity of nanostructured BiSbTe at 350 K falls below 0.60 W/mK after Wiedemann-Franz decoupling.
rationale: Deterministic WF decoupling of both records yields kappa_l 0.56-0.53 W/mK, consistent with intensified boundary scattering in nanostructured microstructures.

statement: Na-doped PbTe retains sigma >= 1.0e5 S/m up to 750 K so that the reported zT 1.4 is achieved without carrier collapse.
rationale: The excerpt reports zT 1.4 @ 750 K but room-temperature transport only; the audit flags a 48% zT mismatch at 300 K, so high-temperature sigma retention is the decisive unverified link.

statement: SnSe b-axis room-temperature electrical conductivity is below 10 S/m, limiting near-RT zT despite very high Seebeck coefficient.
rationale: Reported sigma 0.09 S/cm (= 9 S/m) with S = +450 uV/K gives a large power factor penalty at 300 K.

statement: SnSe lattice thermal conductivity stays below 0.35 W/mK up to 973 K along the b axis.
rationale: The 0.23 W/mK lattice value at 973 K is reported only as kappa_l; total kappa has not been extracted, so the claim awaits total-kappa measurement to be decoupled programmatically.
